package_info.why_malicious: The package contains an OS command injection vulnerability (CVE-2021-21315) that allows attackers to execute arbitrary system commands by passing unsanitized input to backend functions. This can lead to full system compromise if exploited.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Passes user-controlled containerID directly to a function that ultimately executes a system command, without sanitization.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: User input (containerID) is used directly in a context that leads to OS command execution, enabling command injection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would sanitize or validate all user input before using it in system commands. Here, input is used unsanitized.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would involve only trusted, validated input (e.g., internal IDs) and never raw user input.
key_indicators: Direct use of user input in command execution
Lack of input type checking or sanitization
No validation for prototype pollution or malicious payloads

attack_chain.action: Attacker supplies a malicious containerID parameter to a backend API or function using systeminformation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Unsanitized input is passed to a system command execution context.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable function (dockerContainerInspect) passes the malicious input to _docker_socket.getInspect, which executes a system command.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary OS command execution with the privileges of the Node.js process.

behavioral_signatures: User-controlled input passed to system command execution functions
Lack of input sanitization or type checking before command execution
Unexpected command execution patterns in backend Node.js processes
file_indicators: Functions that call getInspect or similar with unsanitized parameters
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections initiated by Node.js processes
Unexpected network activity following API calls with user-supplied parameters
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Audit code for instances where user input is passed to system command execution functions (e.g., child_process.exec, getInspect) without proper sanitization or type checking. Monitor runtime logs for unexpected command execution or errors related to malformed input. Use static analysis tools to flag unsanitized input flows to sensitive sinks.
